question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200; resource https://mcp.vercel.com/; resource_name Vercel MCP; authorization_servers: https://vercel.com; scopes_supported: openid (one scope); resource_documentation https://vercel.com/docs/mcp/vercel-mcp; organization, description and logo fields present
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://vercel.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (an OpenID provider document as well: jwks_uri, claims_supported, id_token_signing_alg RS256); registration_endpoint present (api.vercel.com/login/oauth/register); scopes_supported openid, email, profile, offline_access; PKCE S256; grants authorization_code, client_credentials, refresh_token, device_code; token auth client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, client_secret_jwt, private_key_jwt (no public-client method); response_modes_supported web_message.opener only; a session cookie set on the GET is redacted in the transcript
decoded.rest: GET https://api.vercel.com/v2/user with no Authorization header answers 403 (not 401) with code forbidden, message: The request is missing an authentication token, missingToken true, and no www-authenticate

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.vercel.com answers 401 with a Bearer challenge (error invalid_token, a description, the protected-resource metadata URL, no realm) and the same error as JSON. The metadata names vercel.com as the authorization server with one scope, openid, and carries a resource name, documentation link and description. vercel.com's server document doubles as an OpenID provider document and advertises dynamic registration at api.vercel.com, PKCE S256, four grants including client_credentials and device_code, and four confidential token-auth methods with no public-client method (none is absent), which is the opposite of Stripe's server the same afternoon. Its only response mode is web_message.opener, a browser-window mode. A keyless GET on the REST API answers 403 rather than 401, with a body saying the authentication token is missing and no challenge header. Same challenge shape as the 2026-09-12 measurement in the entry's notes; the grant and auth-method lists are recorded here for the first time. Nothing here measures what either server does with a credential.
